title: SNO: Securing Network Function Offloading on FPGA-based SmartNICs in Untrusted Clouds
problem: FPGA-based SmartNICs offload network functions but lack security guarantees for untrusted clouds; existing FPGA TEEs fail to provide packet I/O protection and user-friendly memory access, forcing users to trust cloud service providers.
motivation: SmartNICs enable efficient network function offloading; securing them in untrusted clouds is critical for cloud users handling sensitive network traffic.
method: SNO protects FPGA-based network processing using three security components. Secure boot ensures trusted code loads without being tampered with. SNO Manager verifies the right code is running (attestation) and orchestrates the system alongside the CPU's trusted environment. SNO Guard encrypts and authenticates all packets using AES-GCM with a pipelined design—operations overlap to minimize slowdown.
key_novelty: SNO is the first trusted execution environment for FPGA-based SmartNICs that combines secure boot, attestation (proof the right code is running), and encrypted packet protection without major performance overhead.
contributions: Secure boot and attestation for FPGA SmartNICs
86.9% user code reduction vs. manual implementation
limitations: Evaluation limited to five network functions; threat model constraints not fully specified; scalability to higher-throughput scenarios unclear.
